title.title: A uniform Laughlin gap, stable under weak disorder
title.subtitle: Claim: above the Laughlin state at filling $1/3$ the gap is at least $1/25$ for all large $N$

beats.text: Electrons in the lowest Landau level at filling $1/3$, with the $V_1$ interaction
The Laughlin state has energy zero; every other state sits above a gap
Claim: the gap stays at least $1/25$ for all large $N$, so it never closes

achievement.label: Laughlin spectral-gap conjecture (Haldane 1983)
achievement.context: Before: only truncated thin-cylinder and torus models (Nachtergaele–Warzel–Young 2021)
achievement.note: Also stable under weak bounded disorder, with existential constants

verify.detail: Lean: the uniform gap and $H^2 \ge \gamma H$. Not stability under disorder
verify.ourCheck: We compared the Lean scope with the claim; we did not build it

sources.quote: the gap above the Laughlin state is at least 1/25 for all large N

plain: Electrons in a strong magnetic field form a stiff quantum fluid; this claims its energy gap never closes

steps: Turn the gap question into one operator inequality
Prove it piece by piece, splitting states by particles and holes
It holds at every size, so the gap never closes

voice.text: The Laughlin state has zero energy. Every other state sits above a gap.
One operator inequality gives the gap, proved by splitting particles and holes.
Claimed: at least one twenty-fifth, for all sizes.
